independent.summary: In findOrCreateGroup, the `proposed-target` path trusts `p.targetGroupId` without re-checking that the group still holds the proposal's members: a member the group does not hold is silently skipped (`if (!held) continue`), yet the back-reference `$addToSet` is still written for every member and the item is recorded `applied`. Reachable two ways — (a) a human removes a member from a 3+-member group between draft creation and apply (DELETE /relationship-groups/:id/members/:entityId leaves the group alive and pulls the back-ref), so the re-import neither restores the edge nor reports a problem and leaves the entity with a `relationships` entry for a group it is not in (inflating the list view's link count); (b) an API-level edit (PATCH /drafts/:id/items/:itemId with decision 'edited') may re-point `members` while keeping `targetGroupId`, which `relationshipPayloadSchema` accepts — the applier then writes nothing of the accepted edit, bumps back-refs on entities the group does not contain, and still returns success. The apply-time matcher path cannot hit this (it requires containment); only the id-targeted path lacks the check the comment on line 261 assumes ("cannot happen under the match rule").

grades.reason: Never shrinking a matched group is the item's explicit requirement ("never removing a member a human added") and proposing removals is listed out of scope as drift detection, so the described behaviour is the specified design, not a defect.

normalizeDraft only proposes — it writes nothing — so member-label updating is not that test's subject, and the suite does assert the re-spelled role is carried on `proposed.members[0].label` while the apply-side `$set` (including resetting a hand-written 'Neighbour' to 'Dependency') is verified in server/tests/http/composeDraft.test.js.

Same misreading as finding 2 applied to the OpenAPI parse test: a producer unit test cannot verify an apply-time `$set`, and that behaviour is covered by the http apply test, so the test does test what it claims.

triageGrades.reason: No session, passkey, permission or actor logic is modified; workspace scoping is reused as-is.
No credential handling, redaction or export-secret code is touched.
No allowance, usage-meter or pricing code is in the diff; the file-producer routes remain unmetered.

The change introduces an in-place overwrite of pre-existing data — `$set` on an existing RelationshipGroup member's `label`/`notes`, with no ChangeLog for relationship writes — and its own test asserts a hand-written role ('Neighbour') is reset to the file's value, so destructive writes are squarely touched.
No outbound HTTP or third-party provider call is added or changed; parsing stays local.
Only an additive enum value and an optional payload field; no version, deploy config or migration is involved.

summary: The local review found nothing real — one finding restates the item's explicit out-of-scope decision, two are duplicate test-coverage complaints that misattribute apply-time behaviour to parse-time unit tests — and it also mis-triaged the in-place overwrite of existing relationship-group members as non-destructive while missing the unvalidated `targetGroupId` apply path.
